pinterest.title: Are Lab Grown Diamonds Worth It? An Unsold Guide to Lab-Grown vs Natural
pinterest.description: Lab grown diamonds are real diamond, with the same crystal structure as a mined stone and nearly the same chemical, optical and physical properties. What differs is growth history, rarity and the story behind the stone. This guide separates settled fact from genuine uncertainty, explains why neither stone should be bought as an investment, and lists the paperwork to insist on either way.

pinterest.title: Lab-Grown Diamond Engagement Rings: Worth It If, Think Twice If
pinterest.description: Deciding on lab grown diamond engagement rings? A balanced checklist. Worth it if you want the look you love and would rather put the difference towards the proposal, honeymoon or wedding. Think twice if a natural origin or an heirloom story matters most. Either way, ask for origin in writing, a report number you have checked on the lab's own site, and the girdle inscription seen under a loupe.

slides: Are lab-grown diamonds worth it? A straight answer from people who sell neither stone.
Yes, it is real diamond. Same crystal structure as a mined stone, nearly the same chemical, optical and physical properties. Only the growth history differs.
Not the same as cubic zirconia or moissanite. Those are simulants, unrelated to diamond at the atomic level.
Can you tell by eye? No. Labs separate lab-grown and natural with screening equipment and spectroscopic testing.

instagram_carousel.caption:
Lab-grown or natural? If you can comfortably choose either, the real question is which one gives you what you actually care about.

Here is what is settled. A lab-grown diamond is real diamond, with the same crystal structure as a mined stone and nearly the same chemical, optical and physical properties. Both sit at 10 on the Mohs scale. To the naked eye they can be indistinguishable; labs tell them apart by growth history.

Here is what differs. Natural stones carry a natural origin and a very different growth history. Lab-grown stones are offered at a reduced price point. Neither should be bought as an investment, so if resale matters, ask about buy-back or upgrade terms in writing before you pay.

And be wary of vague green claims. Words like "sustainable" or "eco-friendly" need evidence, so ask for it in writing.

Whichever you choose, insist on: origin in writing next to the word "diamond", a report number you have checked on the lab's own site, and the girdle inscription seen under a loupe and matched to the report.

The full guide (lab-grown vs natural, HPHT and CVD, grading reports and a worth it / think twice checklist) is at the link in our bio.
